title: Loops inside loops
summary: The inner loop runs in full every time; shapes, pairs and grids. Delve gets a map, drawn row by row, with fog over what you have not seen.

steps.title: The inner loop runs in full, every time
body: Put a loop inside another and the **inner loop runs completely for each pass of the outer one**. Think of a clock: the minute hand goes all the way round for every single step of the hour hand.
If the outer loop runs 3 times and the inner 4, the inner body runs 3 × 4 = 12 times.
Python      for r in range(1, 4): for c in range(1, 5): ...
Step through and watch `c` reset to 1 each time `r` moves on.

steps.prompt: A times table. What is printed? (Trailing spaces do not matter.)
steps.explain: Each row is one pass of `r`. Inside it, `c` runs 1, 2, 3 and the `WriteLine` ends the row.
5 outer passes × 4 inner passes. Nested loops multiply; that is why they get slow on big inputs.

steps.title: When the inner loop depends on the outer
body: The inner loop's bounds may use the outer counter. That makes triangles, and it is how you visit **every pair once**:
for j from i+1 to n-1      j always starts after i
compare item i with item j
Starting `j` at `i + 1` skips comparing an item with itself and skips pairs already seen in the other order.

steps.prompt: The inner loop's end uses `row`. What shape is printed?
Every pair once. What is printed?
code: for (int j = i + 1; j < names.Length; j++)
steps.explain: Three people make three pairs. With `j` starting at 0 you would also get `Ann-Ann`, `Bo-Ann` and so on: nine lines.

steps.prompt: Print a 3 by 5 rectangle of `#`: three rows of five.

steps.title: Has a duplicate?
prompt: Write `bool HasDuplicate(int[] nums)` that returns `true` if any value appears twice. Use two nested loops that compare every pair once.
solution: for (int j = i + 1; j < nums.Length; j++)
template: Dojo.Eq("{ 7 } (one item never duplicates)", false, HasDuplicate(new[] { 7 }));
hints: If `j` starts at 0 you compare each item with itself and always find a "duplicate".
Start the inner loop at `j = i + 1`, and return `true` as soon as two match.

steps.title: Staircase
prompt: Write `string Stairs(int n)` returning a right-aligned staircase of `n` rows, rows joined by `\n` (no newline at the end). Row `k` (from 1) has `n - k` spaces then `k` `#`.
solution: for (int s = 0; s < n - k; s++) sb.Append(' ');
for (int h = 0; h < k; h++) sb.Append('#');
hints: One outer loop for the rows, two inner loops one after the other: spaces, then hashes.

steps.title: Draw the map
prompt: Write **`static string Render(string[] map, bool[,] seen, int heroX, int heroY)`**, which Delve prints after every move. `map[y][x]` is the tile at column `x` of row `y`; `seen[y, x]` is `true` once the hero has seen that tile (a `bool[,]` is a grid of boxes: row first, then column).
For each row, and in it each column:
- the hero's position prints `'@'` (even if it is not seen yet)
- an unseen tile prints `' '` (a space: fog)
Rows are joined with `'\n'`, with **no newline after the last row**. A `StringBuilder` collects the characters: `sb.Append('#')`, then `sb.ToString()`.
starter: static string Render(string[] map, bool[,] seen, int heroX, int heroY)
solution: static string Render(string[] map, bool[,] seen, int heroX, int heroY)
template: for (int r = 0; r < 3; r++) for (int c = 0; c < 5; c++) dojoAll[r, c] = true;
Dojo.Eq("everything seen, hero at (1, 1)", "#####\n#@.>#\n#####", Render(dojoMap, dojoAll, 1, 1));
Dojo.Eq("the hero moves to (2, 1)", "#####\n#.@>#\n#####", Render(dojoMap, dojoAll, 2, 1));
dojoSome[0, 0] = true; dojoSome[0, 1] = true; dojoSome[0, 2] = true;
Dojo.Eq("fog where nothing is seen", "###  \n#@.  \n     ", Render(dojoMap, dojoSome, 1, 1));
Dojo.Eq("nothing seen: only the hero shows", "     \n  @  \n     ", Render(dojoMap, new bool[3, 5], 2, 1));
Dojo.Eq("one row, one column", "@", Render(new[] { "." }, new bool[1, 1], 0, 0));
Dojo.Check("no newline after the last row", !Render(dojoMap, dojoAll, 1, 1).EndsWith("\n"), "the last row ends the text");

require.message: Uses a loop inside a loop

forbid.message: Every function starts with `static` (Delve keeps its pieces in one static class)

hints: Outer loop over `y` (rows), inner loop over `x` (columns), exactly like the rectangle of `#`.
Three cases for each cell, in order: the hero, a seen tile, fog. Append one character for each.
The newline goes after each row except the last: `if (y < map.Length - 1) sb.Append('\n');`

build.title: The map
build.unlocks: Delve draws its map now, and the fog lifts as you explore.
